title: Degraded-mode scheduling and adaptive readiness throttles for SLO resilience
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Problem statement: We intermittently observe SLO degradation in multi-tenant serving pools when transient backend slowdowns coincide with aggressive autoscaler reactions. Current readiness/liveness probes are binary and tightly coupled to the autoscaler, which causes cascading evictions or overprovisioning depending on the signal noise.

Goal: Implement a graded readiness model and coordinated degraded-mode scheduling so that (1) transient tail-latency events are handled via short-lived shedding/circuit breaks instead of immediate instance termination, (2) autoscaler inputs are smoothed by a multi-window health score, and (3) low-priority or opportunistic traffic can be shed predictably to protect high-priority SLOs.

Scope: runtime-level readiness refactor + autoscaler input surface changes + rollout plan for hosted and Dedicated pools. This ticket covers design, telemetry, feature flag rollout, and initial canary. Implementation subtasks cover probe classification, circuit-breaker state machine, autoscaler smoothing, and dashboarding.

Non-goals: full multi-region routing policy changes (will follow in a separate project), model-level quality fallback orchestration (handled by Optimize/Console teams).
acceptance_criteria: Introduce graded readiness states (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) with documented semantics and expose via /healthv2 endpoint
Autoscaler consumes composite health score windowed over 30s/5m/15m with hysteresis to avoid flapping
Circuit-breaker isolates noisy instances for 60-300s based on failing score and causes token-aware shedding instead of immediate kill
End-to-end canary: 10% of requests in a non-critical cluster use the new readiness logic with metrics showing reduced instance churn and no SLO regressions
Dashboards updated to show health score breakdown, circuit-breaker states, and shed rate by priority
design_notes:
Key ideas: 1) Replace binary readiness probe with a 3-tier health score derived from latency percentiles, error rates, and KV cache eviction spikes; 2) Use a probabilistic short-circuit (circuit-breaker) that routes low-priority requests to fallback model-variants or returns fast 503s while keeping high-priority traffic routed; 3) Autoscaler will base decisions on the aggregated health score with configurable derating factors per pool; 4) Provide emergency 'quarantine' mode that isolates a subset of instances for deeper debugging without impacting overall pool stability.

Trade-offs: More signals increase complexity and risk of misconfiguration; to mitigate we introduce sane defaults and guardrails (max shed rate, min healthy capacity). We keep the legacy /health endpoint for backwards compatibility and introduce /healthv2 for new logic.

Telemetry: Add metrics health_score{window="30s|5m|15m"}, cb_state{instance, pool}, shed_rate{priority}, instance_quarantine_count. Required dashboards and SLO burn rate charts are listed in the rollout plan.

References: Confluence design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Graded+Readiness+and+Degraded+Scheduling , Kernel/Runtime PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1219
implementation_plan:
1) Probe refactor: implement health aggregator in runtime (ENG-78124). 2) Circuit-breaker: add CB state machine and token-aware shedding rules (ENG-78125). 3) Autoscaler: update input pipeline and smoothing windows, add derating knobs (ENG-78126). 4) Telemetry: emit new metrics and create dashboards. 5) Canary: gate behind feature flag and deploy to us-west non-critical pool (10% traffic). 6) Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% after stability checks.

Estimate breakdown: probe refactor (2), circuit-breaker (3), autoscaler changes (3), telemetry/dashboards (2), canary/runbook (1).
rollout_runbook: Canary target: us-west-nonprod -> Step 0: enable feature flag in runtime config for 10% of requests in target pool. Step 1 (0-30m): monitor health_score and instance churn (alerts suppressed for expected behavioral differences). Step 2 (30m-2h): verify shed_rate for low-priority traffic < 10% and no increase in 99th latency for high-priority. Step 3 (2h-24h): check burn rate and error budgets; confirm no increase in customer-facing errors. If metrics show high instance churn or SLO violations, rollback flag to off. Major rollout gated on SLO safe signals for 48h. Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Degraded+Mode+Runbook
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Mis-tuned thresholds cause premature shedding and customer impact. Mitigation: conservative defaults, manual override flags, and initial canary in non-critical pools. Risk: Autoscaler hysteresis delays needed scale-ups during true sustained load. Mitigation: allow manual override of derating and ensure autoscaler still observes raw capacity metrics. Risk: increased observability noise. Mitigation: structured logs and new dashboards to separate probe noise from genuine regressions.
